Your [Invoxia](https://www.invoxia.com/) GPS trackers (bike, car, pets,
luggage...) in Gladys, through the cloud of Invoxia, with the account of the
Invoxia app.

- each tracker becomes a Gladys device: **latitude**, **longitude**,
  **accuracy** (m), **battery** (%), **moving** (when the tracker gives it),
  **last seen** and **silent**;
- a scene trigger **Tracker silent**: no news from the tracker for 1 hour to
  48 hours (chosen in the scene): flat battery, tracker removed, no network.

Read only, by polling: Gladys reads the cloud of Invoxia at a regular
interval and never changes anything at Invoxia (mode, alerts and zones stay
in the app).

> **This integration has never been tested with a real Invoxia tracker nor a
> real account.** This first version was written from the
> [gps-tracker](https://gitlab.com/ezlo.picori/gps_tracker) library (MIT),
> ported to JavaScript, and tested against a fake Invoxia API only. Tell the
> Gladys forum what works and what does not.

Unofficial integration, not affiliated with Invoxia.

## An access to use gently

Invoxia offers no API to its consumer customers (it is kept for its
professional offer). Like gps-tracker, this integration uses the API of the
Invoxia app with your credentials. According to the author of gps-tracker,
the terms of use of Invoxia do not forbid it outright, but do not encourage
it either, and Invoxia could act on an account that abuses it. The integration therefore keeps the requests to the bare
minimum: 5 minutes at least between two readings, and the location of a
tracker is read again only when its status changed.

## Configuration

- **E-mail address** and **Password**: those of your Invoxia account (the
  Invoxia app). The password is kept by Gladys in its database, never shown
  again, never written to a log, and sent only to the Invoxia API
  (`https://labs.invoxia.io`, over https, certificate checked). The e-mail
  address is never written to a log either.
- **Refresh**: every 5 minutes to every hour (5 minutes by default). One
  request per reading, plus one per tracker whose position changed. The
  trackers themselves report only every few minutes to every few hours
  (depending on their mode, to save their battery): reading more often
  would bring nothing.
- **Silent after**: 1 hour to 48 hours (24 hours by default): the delay
  without news after which the **Silent** feature turns on.

Then open the **Discovery** tab and create the trackers to follow. Only the
created trackers receive their values.

## What each feature shows

- **Latitude / Longitude**: the last known position, in degrees, rounded to
  6 decimals. Both always go together. The newer of the last location of
  the tracker and of the position given by its status. No history by
  default (privacy; you can turn it on in the device).
- **Accuracy** (m): the accuracy of the last location, as Invoxia gives it.
  No history by default.
- **Battery** (%): the battery of the tracker.
- **Moving** (1 / 0): read from the `stationary` field of the status of the
  tracker (0: moving, above 0: still, -1: unknown). **Reading to be
  confirmed** on a real tracker. The feature appears in Discovery only once
  the value was seen for this tracker (then update the created device to
  add it).
- **Last seen**: the last news from the tracker (its last event or its last
  position), as `2026-10-18 08:00 UTC` (UTC: the integration does not know
  the time zone of Gladys).
- **Silent** (1 / 0): no news for the delay of the configuration.
- A value Invoxia does not give is not published. Gladys accepts 300 states
  per minute from an integration: this one sends 250 at most.

## Scene trigger: Tracker silent

Choose the tracker (or any) and the delay (**required**: 1 hour to 48
hours). The scene starts when the tracker gave no news for this delay, at
the next reading. Only the trackers created in Gladys fire. **Once per
silence**: newer news (even old) arms again only the delays longer than
its age. Never for a delay
already reached when the integration starts (no event at the first
reading), nor for a tracker seen for the first time, nor at a reading where
the clock of Gladys jumped. 30 events at most per reading. Variables: name
of the tracker, silent for (minutes), last seen.

## Connection problems

- **Credentials refused** (HTTP 401 or 403 of the Invoxia API on the list
  of trackers, or two 401 in a row on the positions; a single 401 on a
  position only makes that tracker wait): a wrong password tried again and again may lock the
  account. Gladys therefore stops for **1 hour**, then **6 hours**, then
  **24 hours** after each new refusal, never in a loop. The stop is kept in
  `/data`: a restart, a reconnection of Gladys and the test button wait
  too. An attempt still in flight when the integration stops counts as a
  refusal. Saving the configuration with the same credentials makes **one**
  attempt at once per series of refusals; other credentials are tried at
  once. A reading that works forgets the refusals.
- **Invoxia overloaded** (HTTP 429, on any request) or **server error**
  (HTTP 5xx on the list of trackers): every request is paused, for the time
  Invoxia asks (Retry-After) between 1 minute and 6 hours, never less than
  the refresh. The pause is kept in `/data`, even when the answer arrives
  during a reconnection of Gladys. When it happens on the reading of a
  position, the status of the trackers (battery, last seen) is published
  first.
- **The position of one tracker fails** (HTTP 5xx, timeout): only that
  tracker waits (2, 4, 8, then 16 readings at most, or until its status
  changes); the other trackers keep their position and the integration
  stays connected. When several trackers fail in the same reading, the
  whole reading fails (a pause for a 5xx, a retry otherwise). A position
  refused (HTTP 403, 404, unreadable answer: a tracker without a
  subscription?) is left as it was until the status of the tracker changes.
- **Access refused by something else than the API** (a 403 page of a
  firewall or a proxy), **unexpected answer**, **Invoxia unreachable**
  (network, 30 s timeout, certificate): retried after the refresh, then the
  delay doubles up to 1 hour, even after a restart of the integration (the
  wait is kept in `/data`). The integration never gives up.
- **A date more than a day in the future** (a tracker with a wrong clock)
  is ignored: only the other dates count for "last seen" and "silent".
- **Test the connection** reads again and says how many trackers answer; it
  never shortens a stop nor a pause.

## Privacy

No position, no tracker name or id, neither the e-mail address nor the
password is ever written to a log or to the `/data` volume of the
integration (it keeps there only a short digest of the credentials, 4
characters, used only to see that they changed, with the end of a stop, of
a pause or of a wait). The integration keeps the positions in memory only;
Gladys keeps the last position of each tracker in its database (and its
backups), and the whole history only if you turn it on. The external id of
a device is a non-secret digest of the Invoxia id of the tracker (never the
id itself nor the serial number).

## Limits

- **Gladys does not move a Gladys user on its map from a tracker**: an
  integration cannot publish the position of a user today (as for
  PhoneTrack). A request is open on Gladys:
  [https://github.com/GladysAssistant/Gladys/issues/3224](https://github.com/GladysAssistant/Gladys/issues/3224). Until then, the
  zones of Gladys do not react to the trackers.
- One account per integration, 20 trackers at most (the trackers created in
  Gladys first).
- Nothing is commanded: neither the mode of the tracker, nor the "lost"
  mode, nor the alerts.
- Never tested with a real tracker: see TODO.md in the repository.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Invoxia asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| How it works | `section` | No | Gladys reads your Invoxia GPS trackers through the cloud of Invoxia, with the account of the Invoxia app. Each tracker becomes a Gladys device (Discovery tab): latitude, longitude, accuracy, battery, moving (when the tracker gives it), last seen and silent. Read only: Gladys never changes anything in Invoxia. Gladys does not move the position of a Gladys user on its map yet (see the documentation). Invoxia does not offer this access to its customers: it is the one of its app, used gently (5 minutes between two readings at least). Never tested with a real tracker. Unofficial integration, not affiliated with Invoxia. |
| E-mail address | `string` | Yes | The e-mail address of your Invoxia account (the one of the Invoxia app). Never logged. |
| Password | `secret` | Yes | The password of your Invoxia account. Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, never logged, sent only to the Invoxia API. |
| Refresh | `select` | Yes | How often Gladys reads the trackers (one request, plus one per tracker whose position changed). The trackers themselves report only every few minutes to every few hours, to save their battery. |
| Silent after | `select` | Yes | A tracker that gave no news for this long is shown silent (feature Silent). The scene trigger has its own choice. |

## How to install Invoxia in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Invoxia appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-invoxia:0.1.2`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-invoxia](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-invoxia).

Invoxia requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Invoxia is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), not by the Gladys core team.
